result: The study identified an average of 44,238 H3K27ac-positive and 74,325 H3K4me1-positive genomic regions, 12,157 active genes (FPKM ≥1), and 27,162 chromatin loops from term-pregnant, nonlabor myometrial biopsies using ChIP-seq, RNA-Seq, and Hi-C assays.
evaluation: All reviewers acknowledged the multi-omics approach as a strength. Reviewer 1 stated the 'data presented to support the main conclusion are solid,' and Reviewer 2 noted 'several genome-wide data sets are generated from the same patient samples.' While Reviewer 2 requested more extensive Hi-C analysis, the basic data generation was not questioned.

result: Comparison with previous studies revealed significant variability in H3K27ac-positive intervals across samples, with only 8,563 common regions identified between studies, constituting 20.7-71.5% of total intervals depending on the sample.
evaluation: Reviewer 1 explicitly identified 'variability in epigenomic mapping' as a weakness, stating 'significant variations in the number and location of H3K27ac-positive intervals across different samples and studies suggest potential challenges in accurately mapping the myometrial epigenome.' This variability was acknowledged but raised concerns about interpretation robustness and generalizability.

result: Among three specimens, 13,114 putative enhancers (H3K27ac and H3K4me1 double-positive) were commonly identified, with more than one-third located within 100 kb of high-expressing genes (FPKM≥15) and 13.3% associated with low-expressing genes.
evaluation: Reviewers accepted the identification and characterization of putative enhancers. Reviewer 3 noted the study 'linking putative enhancers and super enhancers to gene expression levels' as a contribution. No specific critiques were raised about these enhancer identification claims.

result: Motif enrichment analysis revealed overrepresentation of binding motifs for myometrial transcription factors (AP-1, STAT5, NFκB), steroid hormone receptors (PGR, NR3C1), and smooth muscle regulators (SRF, ELK1), suggesting integration of smooth muscle and hormonal control programs.
evaluation: Reviewers did not challenge the motif enrichment findings. Reviewer 1 noted the identification of 'myometrial cis-acting elements and their association with gene expression' as a strength. The analysis approach was accepted, though Reviewer 1 questioned why 'regular enhancers are being understood in terms of motif enrichment of transcription factors and super-enhancers in terms of pathways,' suggesting analytical inconsistency rather than data quality issues.

result: 540 putative super enhancers were commonly identified across three subjects, with >40% located within 100 kb of high-expressing genes (FPKM≥15) and 76% co-localizing with known PGR-occupied regions, compared to 20% co-localization in regular enhancers.
evaluation: The super enhancer identification and PGR co-localization findings were accepted by reviewers. Reviewer 1 acknowledged the study's contribution in identifying 'myometrial cis-acting elements and their association with gene expression, particularly the regulation of the PLCL2 gene by PGR.' No specific critiques were raised about these super enhancer characterization claims.

result: Genes associated with putative super enhancers showed enrichment for functions in cytoskeleton organization, extracellular-receptor interaction, transcription regulation, mRNA stability, and estrogen signaling.
evaluation: Reviewers accepted the functional enrichment analysis. Reviewer 1 noted the identification of regulatory programs, though commenting that 'the exact mechanisms by which these enhancers regulate gene expression and cellular functions in the myometrium remain unclear,' indicating acceptance of the associations but calling for deeper mechanistic studies.

result: Hi-C analysis identified a chromatin loop at the PLCL2 locus spanning ~90 kb upstream of the TSS, containing seven H3K27ac-marked regions in all three specimens, six of which co-localized with transcription regulator occupancy sites from the ReMap Atlas.
evaluation: Reviewer 2 explicitly criticized the Hi-C analysis as superficial, stating 'there is minimal description in the results section of the Hi-C data analysis and the only data shown are the number of loops identified and one such loop.' They requested 'more extensive analysis of the Hi-C data, for example, the analysis of TADs,' and in revision comments noted 'the superficial nature of the Hi-C analysis were not addressed.'

result: CRISPRa screening identified multiple gRNAs (PLCL2-1, -3, -5, -6, -7, -8) that significantly increased PLCL2 expression in hTERT-HM cells, with PLCL2-5 showing the greatest effect and functioning in both hTERT-HM and T-HESC cells, supporting the PLCL2-5-targeted region as a cis-acting element.
evaluation: Reviewers praised the functional screening approach. Reviewer 1 stated 'They have used CRISPRa-based screening of PLCL2 gene regulation using immortalized human cell-line hTERT-HM and T-hESC to add more dimension to the work which strengthens their finding.' Reviewer 3 noted 'the use of CRISPR activation system to specifically target cis-acting elements' as a strength.

result: PGR overexpression increased PLCL2 mRNA in hTERT-HM cells, and inferred PGR activity positively correlated (r=0.47) with PLCL2 mRNA levels in 43 human myometrial specimens, supporting PGR as a PLCL2 activator acting through the 35 kb upstream cis-acting element.
evaluation: While reviewers acknowledged the PGR-PLCL2 relationship, Reviewer 2 noted the experiments 'are not as mechanistically integrated as they could be' and requested additional experiments: 'Deletion of the putative enhancer upstream of PLCL2 followed by over-expression of PGR would clarify the mechanistic relationship' and 'reporter assays using this proposed enhancer region with and without increased expression of PGR and mutation of any PRE sequences would also provide mechanistic insight.'

result: The study demonstrates PGR-dependent regulation of PLCL2 in human myometrial cells, suggesting this regulatory pathway is conserved between human and mouse.
evaluation: Reviewers accepted the demonstration of PGR-dependent PLCL2 regulation. Reviewer 1 stated the work 'strengthens their finding of PGR-dependent regulation of the PLCL2 gene in the human myometrial cells.' The conservation claim was not specifically challenged, though mechanistic details were requested.

result: The CRISPRa-based Perturb-Seq assay demonstrated capability to screen cis-acting elements, with 56.7% of cells carrying one detectable gRNA and 27.0% carrying multiple gRNAs, and the dCas9VPR activator generating satisfactory signal-to-noise ratios for single-cell RNAseq detection.
evaluation: Reviewers praised the methodological approach. Reviewer 1 noted the 'comprehensive multi-omic approach, combining ChIP-Seq, RNA-Seq, and CRISPRa-based Perturb-Seq assays' as a strength. Reviewer 3 highlighted 'the combination of ChIP-Seq, RNA-Seq, and CRISPRa Perturb-Seq approaches' as a strength. The technical performance metrics were not questioned.

result: Heterogeneity in cell type compositions due to sampling location, transient presence of genomic regions, and underlying health conditions/medications/environmental factors may contribute to the observed variation in cistromic datasets.
evaluation: These are speculative explanations offered by the authors for observed variability. Reviewer 1 noted 'limited sample size, coupled with variability in results and overall lack of details, compromises the robustness of result interpretation.' Reviewer 1 also stated the study 'focuses on term pregnant nonlabor myometrial specimens, limiting the generalizability of the findings.' These speculations were not directly validated.
